title: Ops cost decoupling and hire acceleration playtest
content:
Executive summary:
- Purpose: run a lightweight experiment that "decouples" short-term ops spend growth from token-price-driven revenue swings by (a) smoothing ops costs via a limited credit pool and (b) accelerating critical hires with a time-bound hire-credit mechanism. Goal is to preserve SLA/backlog targets while reducing forced hiring/layoff churn when token price or committed revenue fluctuates.

Key idea and mechanisms:
- Ops-cost smoothing pool: set aside a rolling credit reserve (in $) to temporarily offset variable GPU/spot costs and short-term contractor spend when token-driven gross margin drops > 12% relative to prior month. Credits expire after 90 days.
- Hire-acceleration credits: award fractional "hire credits" to teams to fast-track 8–12 week critical hires (SWE/Infra/Platform). A hire credit pays for contractor bridge + recruiter premium for up to 12 weeks; team must onboard full-time headcount within 16 weeks to retain.
- Velocity multiplier: when usage growth is > 15% m/m AND utilization > 78% avg, teams can use 1.5x credits to bring forward hires; counterfactual: freeze credits if token price slip > 20% and NRR decline > 3pp.

Assumptions (inputs feeding the sheet):
- Current monthly ops burn (hosted infra + SRE + contractors): $2,140k
- Committed revenue (monthly run-rate): $3,450k
- Token-sensitive variable revenue portion: 32% of run-rate
- Target smoothing pool size: 6 weeks of variable ops (~$330k) as starting tranche
- Average cost to accelerate a hire using credits: $45k (contractor + premium + recruiting)
- Typical ramp-to-productivity: 10 weeks (engineers), 14 weeks (infra/sre)

Scenario outputs (monthly burn, $k) — illustrative:
- Base (no smoothing, no credits): ops burn = 2,140; hiring pace = 6 FTE/mo; deficit when token-price -20% -> additional contingency cut required = $420k
- Smoothing-only (pool = $330k): ops burn effective = 1,980 (pool offsets shortfalls up to 6 weeks); hiring pace = 5 FTE/mo; time-to-adjust = 6 weeks
- Full playtest (pool + hire credits + velocity multiplier): ops burn effective = 2,030; hires accelerated = +2 in Q1; avoided layoffs = estimated 4 FTE over 6 months; 90d cost of credits = $110k

Headcount phasing (playtest cohort: platform & infra priority):
- Q1 target net hires (playtest cohort): 8 (4 platform eng, 2 infra eng, 1 SRE, 1 product ops)
- Onboarding plan: week 0-2 recruiting/shortlist (credit covers premium), week 3-6 contractor bridging, week 7 full-time onboard
- Contingency: if revenue shock triggers pool drawdown > 50% before week 8, hiring pause for non-critical roles and credit repayment clause (pro-rated) for teams

Pricing sensitivity (simple marginal model tied to token price):
- Baseline token price = $0.012/token (effective rev mix assumption)
- Sensitivity test: +/- 10% and +/- 20% price movements; run impact on gross margin and ops-runway
- Example impacts: -10% token price -> gross margin -3.6pp -> need to draw $78k from pool to hold headcount plan; -20% token price -> gross margin -7.2pp -> draw $172k and accelerate cost-conserving measures if pool exhausted

Trigger matrix / runbook (short):
- Trigger A: month-on-month token rev decline > 10% -> auto-notify finance + product + infra (60m SLA), deploy 1: cap hire credits to critical-only, 2: release up to 30% of smoothing pool
- Trigger B: pool drawdown > 50% -> initiate hiring freeze for non-playtest hires; re-evaluate within 2 weeks
- Trigger C: utilization > 85% and backlog > 2w -> allow 1.5x velocity credits; CFO sign-off for > $150k incremental credit spend

Metrics to track (sheet columns):
- Monthly ops burn, variable ops portion, pool balance, credits issued ($), credits consumed ($), hires accelerated (#), hires realized (#), avoided layoffs (#), gross margin delta (pp), runway delta (weeks)

Quantitative example (6-week rolling snapshot):
- Week 1: token rev -8% -> pool draw $42k; credits issued 2 ($90k); hires accelerate 1 SWE
- Week 3: token rev stabilizes; pool balance remaining $198k; recruiter conversion + contractor bridge cost recognized $70k
- Week 6: hires onboarded; avoided 2 layoffs estimated; runway extended by 1.8 weeks vs baseline

Risks and mitigations:
- Moral hazard: teams might game credits to accelerate non-critical hires. Mitigate with strict approval rubric, mandatory hiring-justification doc, and post-hire ROI check at 12 weeks.
- Accounting complexity: credits are off-budget in naive spreadsheets. Mitigate by tagging GL codes and including amortization schedule (credits recognized over 90 days).
- Reversibility: if playtest shows negative unit economics, credits expire and pool is reallocated to contingency reserve.

Operational checklist for pilot:
1) Finance: provision initial pool $330k and create GL tag "smoothing-pool-2026-Q1"
2) People Ops: pre-approve 12-week contractor bridge rate card; escalate recruiter premium policy
3) Product/Infra leads: nominate 6 critical hires and provide justification doc per candidate slot
4) SRE: add utilization dashboard with 7-day rolling avg and backlog heatmap
5) Legal: draft a 90-day credit agreement clause for contractor-to-FTE transitions

Open questions for review meeting:
- Pool sizing: start with 6 weeks vs 8 weeks — tradeoffs?
- Credit expiry window: 90 days vs 120 days impact on conversion rate
- What epsilon of token-price movement should auto-block credits (is 20% the right threshold?)

Next steps (immediate):
- Decision to pilot (yes/no) by 2026-03-10
- Finance to seed pool if approved and add sheet formulas for rolling drawdown and amortization by 2026-03-17
- Run closed 12-week pilot across Platform & Infra; cadence: weekly ops sync + biweekly finance review

Notes to reviewer: this is a working spreadsheet-style playbook, expect iteration. Attached references: capacity runbook (CONFLUENCE-FT:CapacityRunbook-1283), pilot charter (JIRA:FIN-4421).

(End of sheet)
